stem: A shop in Kisumu wants to store thousands of product photos and videos so customers can view them in a web browser. Which Azure Storage service fits best?
why_correct: Blob storage is designed for large amounts of unstructured data such as images and video, and it can serve them straight to a browser.
why_a_wrong: Queues hold messages passed between parts of an application; they are not for storing media files.
why_c_wrong: Tables store structured NoSQL data and are not meant for photos or videos.
why_d_wrong: Disks are block storage volumes attached to Azure virtual machines; they are not used to serve media to browsers.
author: yego

stem: A SACCO wants to keep scanned loan records for several years. The files are almost never opened, and staff can wait for retrieval when they are needed. Which blob access tier gives the lowest storage cost?
why_correct: The Archive tier is meant for data that is rarely accessed, kept for at least 180 days and can tolerate slow retrieval. It has the lowest storage cost of the tiers.
why_a_wrong: Hot is meant for data that is accessed often, so it is a poor fit for records that are rarely opened.
why_b_wrong: Cool is for infrequently accessed data kept at least 30 days, but its storage cost is higher than Archive.
why_d_wrong: Cold is for infrequently accessed data kept at least 90 days, but Archive is the tier built for the rarest access and has the lowest storage cost.
author: yego
